alignments.note: Rule 70: the ASV writes indeed for the correlative μέν.
Rule 17: the periphrasis had been mindful heads on the meaning-bearing complement.
Rules 49 and 17: the substantival demonstrative takes the whole expression including the supplied generic noun, headed on the demonstrative, with the case preposition riding along.
out is the English verb's own particle.

Rule 50: in a counterfactual apodosis the modal answers to ἄν and the perfect auxiliary stays with the lexical verb, as wouldest / have asked does. Discontinuous under rule 15, the modal standing between.
Rule 50: the modal auxiliary of the counterfactual apodosis answers to ἄν, which takes the bare would.
Rule 61: no preposition governs the infinitive, so to is its own rule 7 helper.

review_notes: The accepted alignment gave would have to ἄν and only they … had to εἶχον. Rule 50's own precedent, σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτόν → thou wouldest have asked him, gives the bare modal to the particle and the perfect auxiliary to the verb, so have moves into εἶχον's unit.
εἶχον's unit is discontinuous under rule 15, the ἄν-licensed would standing between they and have had.
